body: [{"streamId":"01a0c941-fb35-746b-a4f4-53979a188e24","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Decision.DecisionRecorded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0c941-fb35-746b-a4f4-53979a188e24\u0022,\u0022Scope\u0022:\u0022Project\u0022,\u0022ScopeId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71\u0022,\u0022Statement\u0022:\u0022**Failed tasks get an explicit human-driven retry: \\u0060h9k task retry\\u0060** (2026-08-17): \\u0060TaskRetried\\u0060 moves a Failed task back to Queued through the decider (Failed-only; Abandoned stays a dead end), preserving lease-generation fencing (the next claim increments as usual, per #7). Origin incident (2026-08-17): the first two automatic follow-up runs completed their work and passed the gates, then died at the daemon\\u0027s plain push against their rebased branches (backlog 08); both tasks fell to Failed, which had no exit, and the completed, gated work sat stranded in the worktrees until it was force-pushed by hand. Failure of the machinery around the work must not permanently condemn the task that contains the work. Design: retry *appends*, never rewrites (the stream reads added \\u2192 \\u2026 \\u2192 failed \\u2192 retried \\u2192 claimed, and \\u0060h9k task show\\u0060 keeps the failure reason alongside the retry reason); it is distinct from \\u0060TaskReopened\\u0060 (Done-only, PR closeout, different guards) rather than overloading one event with both meanings; and it is human-only (the closeout monitor never retries a Failed task automatically: a failure that repeats without human eyes is the never-loop-on-judgment rule, #11), so the event carries no Automatic flag and touches no budget (like \\u0060h9k pr resolve\\u0060, the human asking is the grant). The event records the failed run\\u0027s branch as observed at retry time; the launcher resumes it through the existing follow-up checkout path when it survives (retained worktree first, then local or origin branch) and starts clean from the base branch when the artifacts are gone (never an error, since the retry\\u0027s whole point is recovery). The mechanics also live in the repo-resident **absorb-review-fixes** skill, reusable by hand. The style is a \\u0060CommitStyle\\u0060 value object on the project (\\u0060h9k project set --commit-style narrative|append|default\\u0060), resolved project-over-platform with \\u0060DaemonOptions.DefaultCommitStyle\\u0060 as the platform default (Narrative; user-level defaults arrive with IDEA-platform-defaults); Append keeps the historic stack-on-top behavior. The daemon absorbs the rewrite it now asks for: \\u0060PullRequestOpener\\u0060 pushes follow-up runs (\\u0060RunDispatched.IsFollowUp\\u0060) with \\u0060--force-with-lease\\u0060, never plain \\u0060--force\\u0060; a failed lease means the branch moved on origin and fails the run honestly (no blind retry; \\u0060h9k pr resolve\\u0060 is the requeue lever). The worktree manager treats a diverged resumed branch as rewritten-on-origin and resets the follow-up worktree to the remote tip (the pull request\\u0027s truth; the stale tip stays in the reflog), while a local tip strictly ahead of origin is kept, since that is unpushed work. Branch cleanup already tolerated rewrites (\\u0060-D\\u0060 plus remote delete on the observed merge). Origin incidents (both 2026-08-17): PR #6\\u0027s review round landed as a separate \\u0022harden closeout\\u0022 commit and was rebuilt into the owning commits by hand; the first two automatic follow-up runs then rebased correctly and the daemon\\u0027s plain push failed both (\\u0022failed to push some refs\\u0022), stranding completed, gated work in their worktrees.\u0022,\u0022OriginIncident\u0022:null,\u0022Supersedes\u0022:[],\u0022Provenance\u0022:{\u0022RecordedByOwnerId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5a50-7368-b048-72bcfee948bf\u0022,\u0022RunId\u0022:null,\u0022TaskId\u0022:null,\u0022Attendance\u0022:\u0022Unobserved\u0022,\u0022IsFromRun\u0022:false},\u0022RecordedAt\u0022:\u00222026-09-22T13:15:38.803749\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022LegacyId\u0022:\u0022Decisions Log #26\u0022}","originEventId":"9e4ff920-1a42-4de8-b7b4-336ec2691ef7","originSequence":58824,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-09-22T13:15:39.710928+00:00","originProjectId":"01a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71"},{"streamId":"01a0c941-fb35-746d-acf0-e5e469c20c43","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Decision.DecisionRecorded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0c941-fb35-746d-acf0-e5e469c20c43\u0022,\u0022Scope\u0022:\u0022Project\u0022,\u0022ScopeId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71\u0022,\u0022Statement\u0022:\u0022**Failed is a needs-human waypoint, not a terminal state** (2026-08-18): a failed state means there is an unsolved problem, and an unsolved problem is not an ending. Terminal states say how the story ended; \\u0022ended in failure\\u0022 is only true when a human walks away, which is what Abandoned already means. \\u0060TaskState.IsTerminal\\u0060 is now Done and Abandoned only, and Failed has exactly three human-only exits, which \\u0060h9k task show\\u0060 teaches on any failed task: **retry** (\\u0060h9k task retry\\u0060, re-run, #25), **resolve** (\\u0060h9k task resolve --reason \\u003Cwhy\\u003E [--pr \\u003Curl\\u003E]\\u0060, the new \\u0060TaskResolved\\u0060 event, Failed \\u2192 Done: the human\\u0027s attestation that the objective was met despite the run failure, with the PR URL recording where the work landed), and **abandon** (\\u0060h9k task abandon\\u0060, walk away; previously rejected from Failed because Failed was terminal). The resolve reason is required: an attestation without a why is a guess (the AGENTS.md never-guess rule). Resolve appends, never rewrites: the stream reads added \\u2192 claimed \\u2192 failed \\u2192 resolved, and the failure reason stays visible beside the resolution. Double-Fail stays rejected (\\u0060TaskDecider.CanFail\\u0060, which the daemon\\u0027s failure recorders also use as their pre-check), and Fail from Done or Abandoned still conflicts. \\u0060h9k status\\u0060 counts Failed toward \\u0022need you\\u0022 and ranks it just under NeedsHuman, since it now waits on a human decision. Origin incident (2026-08-18): tasks a282deb0 and 13241bd8 sat Failed although their work merged as PRs #7 and #8. (a) **A parked run structurally holds its task.** #24\\u0027s claim that \\u0022a parked run keeps its task Claimed and its lease alive (adoption refreshes the heartbeat)\\u0022 was false in practice \\u2014 it held only while the heartbeat service was actually ticking, and heartbeat decay (a stopped daemon, a laptop asleep past the 60-second timeout, a wake-up sweep racing the first heartbeat tick) requeued a review-parked task; the platform then rebuilt the same feature from scratch across generations 2-4, roughly tripling the token cost, before gen 5 completed. The correction: the expiry sweep now checks the expired task\\u0027s current run and, when it is ReviewParked (or CloseoutParked \\u2014 the guarantee belongs to \\u0022parked\\u0022, not one flavor), refreshes the lease instead of requeueing. A parked lease can no longer expire into a requeue, on any node, no matter how long the daemon slept. (b) **A verdict-less reviewer gets ONE same-session re-prompt, then parks.** The first live review ended with \\u0022I\\u0027ll deliver findings and the verdict when it completes\\u0022 \\u2014 a promise, not a verdict \\u2014 and parked a finished, correct implementation. The review prompt now forbids ending without the VERDICT line (wait for running checks, then conclude), and the engine resumes a verdict-less session once (\\u0060claude -p --resume\\u0060, the #5 pattern \\u2014 the session already read the diff; a fresh one would re-spend that work) with \\u0060ReviewVerdictReprompted\\u0060 on the stream; a second verdict-less ending parks (never loop on judgment, #11). (c) **\\u0060h9k review resolve\\u0060 is the unpark lever** #24 deliberately deferred, now proven needed (its absence left a parked run no path forward except abandonment): \\u0060--merge-ready\\u0060 sends the run on to PullRequestOpener, \\u0060--needs-fixes \\u003Creason\\u003E\\u0060 dispatches a fix session with the reason as its findings; \\u0060ReviewParkResolved\\u0060 records the human verdict on the run stream, and like \\u0060h9k pr resolve\\u0060 it restores the automatic fix budget \\u2014 the human asking is a fresh grant (#22). The daemon\\u0027s dispatch cycle resumes resolved runs (adoption\\u0027s mid-loop counterpart). (d) **Zero commits fails fast.** Task 08\\u0027s agent completed all its work uncommitted; gates passed vacuously on the unmodified tree and the failure surfaced two stages late as \\u0022No commits between main and branch\\u0022 at PR creation. The verification runner now counts the branch\\u0027s commits past the base before any gate runs and fails the run honestly (\\u0022agent produced no commits\\u0022) \\u2014 except Research tasks, whose deliverable is the transcript (the one TaskType whose legitimate output is empty); an unobservable count is never treated as zero (the gates then surface whatever is actually broken). Retry and follow-up prompts now also tell the agent the retained worktree may already carry a previous attempt\\u0027s work \\u2014 committed or uncommitted \\u2014 to review before starting over, closing the loop that made requeue-from-scratch so expensive.\u0022,\u0022OriginIncident\u0022:null,\u0022Supersedes\u0022:[],\u0022Provenance\u0022:{\u0022RecordedByOwnerId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5a50-7368-b048-72bcfee948bf\u0022,\u0022RunId\u0022:null,\u0022TaskId\u0022:null,\u0022Attendance\u0022:\u0022Unobserved\u0022,\u0022IsFromRun\u0022:false},\u0022RecordedAt\u0022:\u00222026-09-22T13:15:38.803749\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022LegacyId\u0022:\u0022Decisions Log #28\u0022}","originEventId":"0acb2cfc-2c9e-4226-83d8-60f7b3a3b7eb","originSequence":58826,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-09-22T13:15:39.710929+00:00","originProjectId":"01a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71"},{"streamId":"01a0c941-fb35-746f-a39d-f60c3fc83b67","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Decision.DecisionRecorded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0c941-fb35-746f-a39d-f60c3fc83b67\u0022,\u0022Scope\u0022:\u0022Project\u0022,\u0022ScopeId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71\u0022,\u0022Statement\u0022:\u0022**System sleep is not node death** (2026-08-18): a laptop lid-close during two active runs became a generation storm. Each sleep stopped heartbeats; each wake ran the expiry sweep before the heartbeat service\\u0027s first tick; the sweep saw 50-minute-stale leases and requeued both tasks while the previous agents resumed alongside their replacements. Task 13 reached five simultaneous Running generations, four agents sharing one retained worktree, before a human killed the daemon and every agent by hand; roughly three tasks\\u0027 worth of tokens went to building the same two features. Four defenses, all in the dispatch path. (a) **The OS outranks the timestamp for local leases.** Before expiring a lease this node holds, the sweep asks \\u0060IProcessManager\\u0060 whether the current run\\u0027s recorded process is alive (pid \\u002B start time, the #2 identity discipline the adoption path already uses); a live local process means a live lease and a refreshed heartbeat, whatever the heartbeat timestamp says. Remote semantics are unchanged: pids only mean anything on the node that owns them, so a genuinely silent remote lease still expires on the timeout. (b) **Wake detection is a wall-clock comparison, no platform APIs.** The sweep records when it last ran; a gap beyond the expected cadence (PollInterval \\u002B HeartbeatInterval) means the whole daemon, heartbeat service included, was suspended (sleep, debugger pause, VM freeze all look identical), so this node\\u0027s heartbeats are refreshed before expiry is evaluated. The wake-time race between sweeper and heartbeat service is closed structurally, inside the sweep itself, rather than by timing luck. (c) **Single-flight per task per node.** A claim is refused while a previous generation\\u0027s agent process is still alive on this node, closing the duplicate-agent hole from the other side (a requeue that slipped through by hand or before this build). The refusal is per cycle: once the OS reports the process gone, the next claim proceeds. (d) **A merged pull request is never rebuilt.** Before spawning an agent for a task carrying a PR URL, the launcher consults the provider: already merged means the task closes out on the spot (completed with its PR, lease released, worktree and branch cleaned like any closeout) instead of redispatching. Inspection failure falls back to a normal dispatch, since the network is often still down right after a wake. Incident for (d) specifically: after PR #11 merged, the storm-killed generation 5\\u0027s lease expiry requeued the task and generation 6 spawned a fresh agent to rebuild the feature already on main. This narrows but does not replace #28(a): parked runs\\u0027 leases stay alive by design; this keeps RUNNING runs\\u0027 leases honest across suspensions.\u0022,\u0022OriginIncident\u0022:null,\u0022Supersedes\u0022:[],\u0022Provenance\u0022:{\u0022RecordedByOwnerId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5a50-7368-b048-72bcfee948bf\u0022,\u0022RunId\u0022:null,\u0022TaskId\u0022:null,\u0022Attendance\u0022:\u0022Unobserved\u0022,\u0022IsFromRun\u0022:false},\u0022RecordedAt\u0022:\u00222026-09-22T13:15:38.803749\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022LegacyId\u0022:\u0022Decisions Log #29\u0022}","originEventId":"b4ac6b67-a2e6-4151-848e-9933fb15dd9e","originSequence":58827,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-09-22T13:15:39.710929+00:00","originProjectId":"01a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71"},{"streamId":"01a0c941-fb35-7470-96af-b66426ce8569","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Decision.DecisionRecorded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0c941-fb35-7470-96af-b66426ce8569\u0022,\u0022Scope\u0022:\u0022Project\u0022,\u0022ScopeId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71\u0022,\u0022Statement\u0022:\u0022**A run\\u0027s input side is three counts, and cost is observed, never derived** (2026-08-18): \\u0060TokensRecorded\\u0060 read only \\u0060usage.input_tokens\\u0060 from the result payload, which for a cached session is a rounding error. The event now carries \\u0060CacheReadInputTokens\\u0060 and \\u0060CacheCreationInputTokens\\u0060 alongside \\u0060InputTokens\\u0060, appended as defaulted parameters so streams written before they existed replay as zero rather than as a reconstruction (the never-guess rule); \\u0060RunAggregate\\u0060 and \\u0060RunDetails\\u0060 accumulate each count on its own line, and \\u0060TotalInputTokens\\u0060 sums them where a total is what is wanted. The three stay separate rather than lumped because they price differently, so any roll-up that adds them first can never be turned back into money. \\u0060CostUsd\\u0060 remains whatever \\u0060total_cost_usd\\u0060 reported, recorded as observed and never recomputed from the token counts: the platform does not hold a price list, and a computed cost that drifts from the bill is worse than no cost at all. An absent field is zero, never inferred from its siblings. Origin incident (2026-08-18): \\u0060mt_doc_rundetails\\u0060 showed 444,443 output tokens against 822 input tokens across 14 runs, off by about three orders of magnitude, because a resumed session reports nearly all of its input under \\u0060cache_read_input_tokens\\u0060 (one real run: 118 fresh input tokens, 8,239,942 cache-read, 196,080 cache-creation). Any cost report built on those numbers would have been confidently wrong, so the \\u0060h9k stats\\u0060 idea waits until the counts are trustworthy.\u0022,\u0022OriginIncident\u0022:null,\u0022Supersedes\u0022:[],\u0022Provenance\u0022:{\u0022RecordedByOwnerId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5a50-7368-b048-72bcfee948bf\u0022,\u0022RunId\u0022:null,\u0022TaskId\u0022:null,\u0022Attendance\u0022:\u0022Unobserved\u0022,\u0022IsFromRun\u0022:false},\u0022RecordedAt\u0022:\u00222026-09-22T13:15:38.803749\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022LegacyId\u0022:\u0022Decisions Log #30\u0022}","originEventId":"1f533548-4a96-4438-b120-53c98900134a","originSequence":58828,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-09-22T13:15:39.710929+00:00","originProjectId":"01a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71"},{"streamId":"01a0c941-fb35-7471-994d-9b597570490e","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Decision.DecisionRecorded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0c941-fb35-7471-994d-9b597570490e\u0022,\u0022Scope\u0022:\u0022Project\u0022,\u0022ScopeId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71\u0022,\u0022Statement\u0022:\u0022**The daemon has a CLI-owned lifecycle; autostart is a strictly opt-in extra** (2026-08-19, redesigns S1-12): nobody evaluating a local-first tool wants installation to leave a permanently resident background process behind (colleague feedback at the first demo), and the architecture had already paid for the alternative \\u2014 adopt \\u2192 sweep \\u2192 claim at startup plus the closeout sweep mean a stopped daemon costs latency, never correctness, the same trade #29 encoded for sleep. So: **\\u0060h9k install\\u0060 registers nothing** \\u2014 it publishes h9k \\u002B h9kd release binaries to \\u0060~/.hall9k/bin\\u0060 and retargets an existing \\u0060h9k\\u0060 symlink on the PATH (or creates one), idempotently, never clobbering a real file of that name; the \\u0060~/.local/bin\\u0060 fallback is vetted by the same check as every PATH directory, since it is chosen precisely when nothing on the PATH vetted it; re-running after a merge republishes and offers to restart a running daemon, which answers installed-binary staleness (origin incident: the hand-made symlink went stale the moment main advanced). **\\u0060h9k daemon start\\u0060** launches h9kd detached through a \\u0060/bin/sh\\u0060 intermediary that backgrounds the process and exits at once \\u2014 h9kd is reparented to launchd (pid 1) with stdin from /dev/null and stdout/stderr appended to \\u0060~/.hall9k/h9kd.log\\u0060 (read only ever from its tail, and kept inside an 8 MB budget by the daemon itself: a five-minute timer copies the log aside to \\u0060h9kd.log.1\\u0060 and truncates it **in place**, never renames it, because the daemon holds that file\\u0027s descriptor open for its whole lifetime and a rename would send every later line into the rolled-aside generation invisibly, while an O_APPEND writer lands correctly at the start of a truncated one; \\u0060h9k daemon start\\u0060 runs the same rotation before it starts anything. Origin incident (2026-08-19, pre-PR review of this task): rotation ran only on the start path, so an append-only log belonging to a daemon started once and left up for weeks grew for as long as the node lived. The daemon\\u0027s console logging filters Npgsql and Marten to Warning in code, not appsettings.json \\u2014 the installed daemon\\u0027s working directory is never its binary directory, so a published appsettings.json is not read at all \\u2014 which keeps the tail on what the daemon did rather than on SQL), the double-fork pattern with no parent-shell tie (origin incident: the hand-started daemon died three times in one day with its shell). On start the daemon runs an immediate closeout sweep alongside adoption and the lease sweep and logs one **catch-up report** line (\\u0022Catch-up complete \\u2014 adopted N run(s) \\u2026 observed K merge(s)\\u0022), which \\u0060h9k daemon start\\u0060 tails and prints, so the on-demand cost is visible the moment it is paid. **Single instance is enforced twice**: the CLI refuses politely with the running pid, and the daemon itself holds an advisory lock file for its lifetime (pid file carries pid \\u002B start time, the #2 identity discipline) \\u2014 the guard\\u0027s refusal exits 0 deliberately, so a KeepAlive LaunchAgent that loses the race is never thrash-restarted by launchd. **\\u0060h9k daemon stop\\u0060** is SIGTERM-graceful (in-flight event appends finish inside the host\\u0027s 30s shutdown budget; detached agents keep running for adoption, per #2/#7) and goes through \\u0060launchctl bootout\\u0060 whenever launchd owns the job, so stopped always means stopped. **\\u0060h9k daemon autostart enable\\u0060** is the only path to start-at-login: it writes a per-user LaunchAgent (RunAtLoad; KeepAlive with SuccessfulExit=false, so crash-restart never resurrects a clean stop; \\u0060AbandonProcessGroup\\u0060 so tearing the job down never sweeps the detached agents, which share h9kd\\u0027s process group because nothing gives them one of their own and which launchd would otherwise signal along with the job, contradicting the very promise stop prints; origin incident 2026-08-19, cycle-5 pre-PR review of this task) pointing at the installed binary; \\u0060disable\\u0060 fully unregisters. **The registration carries the enabling shell\\u0027s environment** (\\u0060PATH\\u0060 plus whichever \\u0060HALL9K_*\\u0060 overrides are actually set, recorded as observed and never invented), because launchd starts a job from its own environment, whose default \\u0060PATH\\u0060 is \\u0060/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin\\u0060 and holds neither \\u0060claude\\u0060 nor \\u0060gh\\u0060; enable also names any tool the recorded \\u0060PATH\\u0060 cannot resolve. \\u0060disable\\u0060 reports a daemon as stopped only when it saw the pid launchd owned for the job actually go away, since \\u0060bootout\\u0060 succeeds just as happily on a loaded but idle one.
